state.memo_text: To: Executive team. Subject: Northgate warehouse lease. Our Northgate warehouse lease ends in March. The landlord has offered a five-year renewal at a higher rate, and operations has priced an alternative site in Fairview. Decision requested: approve renewing the Northgate lease for five years at the offered rate, or direct operations to pursue the Fairview site instead. Please respond before the next executive meeting.

rationale: After background, the memo names the specific decision it wants: renew Northgate or pursue Fairview.

state.memo_text: Subject: Northgate warehouse. The landlord has sent a renewal offer at a higher rate, and the operations team has looked at a couple of other sites. There is a lot to weigh here and we need a decision from leadership soon. Happy to walk through it whenever convenient.

rationale: The memo says a decision is needed but never states what the reader is asked to approve or which options are on the table.
The memo text is empty, so there is nothing to classify.

state.memo_text: To: Dana Okonkwo, COO (d.okonkwo@tallisgroup.example). Subject: Decision record for the Tallis warehouse lease. After two months of review, the facilities team has made its decision: we are renewing the Tallis lease for three years rather than relocating to the Norrell site or consolidating into the Pendry hub. Both alternatives were weighed and rejected on access and timing grounds, and the decision was signed off within my delegated authority on Tuesday. I am not asking you to decide anything here. What I need from you is to forward this record to the regional leads before Friday's operations call so they hear it from you rather than from the landlord.

rationale: The memo names options and repeats the word decision, but the options were already chosen by the author under delegated authority and are not put to the reader; the only request is to forward the record, which the contract treats as asking for something other than a decision.

state.proposal_text: Proposal: pilot a four-day support schedule in the Halden office. We would run it for one quarter with the existing team and no contract or system changes. If ticket response times slip or the team asks to stop, we return to the five-day schedule at the start of the following month. Requesting approval to start the pilot.

rationale: The proposal describes a trial with a stated way back to the current arrangement.

state.proposal_text: Proposal: sell the Marlow Street building to Corran Holdings. The purchase agreement is binding once signed and contains no buy-back clause; once the sale closes the building cannot be recovered. Proceeds would retire the term loan. Requesting approval to sign.

rationale: The text itself states that the commitment cannot be undone once made.
The proposal text is empty, so reversibility cannot be read.

state.proposal_text: Proposal: enter a supply agreement with Ferrowick Metals for the Marrow product line. Ferrowick has offered us first position on its new alloy capacity, and the offer stands only until the end of the quarter. Waiting is irreversible: if we pass, Ferrowick will allocate that capacity to Corvane Industrial and there will be no second chance to recover our position in the segment. The agreement would cover pricing, volume commitments, and delivery windows, with terms to be finalized by legal. I recommend we sign.

rationale: The only irreversibility language describes the consequence of not acting, not the commitment being asked for; the text never states a way to exit the agreement nor that the agreement is permanent or binding, so it says nothing about undoing the commitment itself.

state.proposal_text: Recommendation: shorten onboarding calls from 60 to 30 minutes. Over the last two quarters, 1,240 onboarding calls averaged 27 minutes of active content, and the 30-minute cohort in the August test showed the same 90-day retention as the 60-minute cohort within survey error. Shortening the slot frees roughly 400 staff hours a quarter.

rationale: The recommendation rests on call counts, measured durations, and a cohort comparison.

state.proposal_text: Recommendation: shorten onboarding calls from 60 to 30 minutes. When I sat in on a call with Brightwell Dental last month we finished everything in twenty minutes and spent the rest on small talk. Two of our onboarding specialists tell me the same thing happens to them. We should shorten the slot.

rationale: The support offered is one observed call and two colleagues' reports, not measured data.
No proposal text is supplied.

state.proposal_text: Recommendation: fund two dedicated onboarding specialists for the Fieldstone enterprise tier, at an estimated annual cost of $240,000, starting in Q1. The case for this is Brindlecote Logistics. Their operations lead, Marisol Venn, told me on our last call that they came close to cancelling because nobody owned their rollout after the sales handoff, and that the only reason they stayed was that an engineer volunteered evenings to walk them through configuration. Anyone who has sat in on an enterprise kickoff knows this is how it goes. Two specialists would take that load off engineering and give each new account a named owner.

rationale: The figures in the text (cost, headcount, start quarter) describe the request itself rather than support for it; the recommendation's support is one named customer's account plus an appeal to what everyone knows, so the strongest kind of support offered is anecdote.

state.proposal_text: Recommendation: replace the in-house billing system with Ledgerline. We also considered keeping the in-house system with a dedicated maintainer, rejected because the two engineers who know it are leaving and rebuilding that knowledge would take longer than migrating. We considered Tallyworks, rejected because it does not support multi-currency invoicing. Doing nothing leaves an unpatched system in place.

rationale: Two other options and doing nothing are named, each with a stated reason for rejection.

state.proposal_text: Recommendation: replace the in-house billing system with Ledgerline. Ledgerline supports multi-currency invoicing, integrates with our ledger, and can be live within two quarters. The migration team is ready to begin. Requesting approval to sign the annual contract.

rationale: Only the recommended course appears; no other option, including doing nothing, is mentioned.
No proposal text is supplied.

state.proposal_text: Proposal: replace the Kessling ticketing system with Orbital Desk across all support regions. We did not run a vendor comparison and have not evaluated any other ticketing platforms; Orbital Desk is the only product the team piloted, and this proposal covers it alone. The one thing we did rule out is leaving Kessling in place, because Kessling's vendor has announced end of support and our security team will not approve running an unsupported system past the current contract year. Migration would be sequenced by region starting with Northwind. I recommend approval.

rationale: Although the text declares that no other platforms were evaluated, it names doing nothing (keeping Kessling) together with a stated reason for rejecting it, and the contract counts doing nothing as a course of action, so at least one alternative is compared.

state.memo_text: Subject: Corvid Labs support contract. Corvid's support contract ends next month. Options: extend for one year on the current terms, or let it lapse and bring support in-house with two new hires. I recommend extending. Please approve one of the two options.

rationale: The memo asks the reader to choose between two named options.

state.memo_text: Subject: Ordering of next year's product work. Before we spend engineering time, I want to confirm the executive team agrees that partner integrations come before the self-serve tier next year. Nothing needs approving yet; I am asking whether anyone objects to that ordering so product planning can proceed on that basis.

rationale: A direction is already stated and the memo asks the readers to confirm agreement or object, not to choose or approve.
The memo text is empty.

state.memo_text: Subject: Support queue consolidation and Q3 figures. Two things. First, we are going to merge the Tier 1 and Tier 2 support queues under Priya Castellan starting next month so that escalations stop bouncing between teams; I want to make sure you are comfortable with that direction before I announce it, so please reply if you see a problem with it. Second, could you send me the Q3 vendor spend report and the current headcount by region? I need both for the board pre-read, and Finance says the versions I have are stale. Nothing here needs sign-off; the queue change is within my remit.

rationale: The memo asks the reader to supply figures and documents (information) and also states a plan and asks the reader to confirm comfort or object with no action to approve (alignment); the contract's stated precedence of decision, then alignment, then information selects alignment.

state.proposal_text: Proposal: open a second fulfillment center in Pellam. Benefits: shorter delivery times to the eastern region and lower freight cost. Risks: if eastern order volume does not grow as forecast, the center runs below half capacity and the fixed lease cost is not covered; hiring in Pellam has been slow for comparable employers, so opening could slip a quarter.

rationale: The text names two specific ways the plan could fail: under-used capacity with uncovered lease cost, and a hiring delay.

state.proposal_text: Proposal: open a second fulfillment center in Pellam. Benefits: shorter delivery times to the eastern region and lower freight cost. As with any expansion there are risks, but the team has reviewed them and considers them manageable. Requesting approval to sign the lease.

rationale: Risk is mentioned only in general terms; no specific downside is named.
No proposal text is supplied.

state.proposal_text: Proposal: launch the Meridian mid-market bundle in the spring cycle with a dedicated sales pod. Risks: as with any launch there is execution risk, and there are the usual uncertainties around timing and adoption, all of which we consider manageable. The real risk is in not launching. If we hold the bundle back another cycle, Corvane Industrial will lock up the mid-market accounts we are targeting, our renewal conversations in that segment will get harder, and the sales pod we have already hired will sit idle. The upside is a new revenue line and a foothold in a segment where we currently have none.

rationale: The specific harms named are consequences of not adopting the plan, not ways the recommended course could fail, cost more, take longer, or cause harm; the plan's own risks are mentioned only as generic manageable execution risk, so no specific downside of the recommended course is stated.

state.proposal_text: Proposal: fund a customer education program for the Atlas product line. Success measure: the share of Atlas accounts that open a how-to support ticket in their first 90 days falls from 38 percent to under 25 percent within two quarters of launch, measured from the support system.

rationale: The text names what is measured, the direction and target of change, and where the number comes from.

state.proposal_text: Proposal: fund a customer education program for the Atlas product line. We will know it has worked when customers feel more confident with the product and the support team spends less time on basic questions. The program would be a clear signal that we invest in our customers.

rationale: Success is described as confidence and less time on basics, with nothing that could be measured as written.

state.proposal_text: Proposal: ship the Fieldstone installer companion app to all certified installers by the end of the year. We will instrument the app from day one and track weekly active installers and completed job checklists, reporting both to this group monthly. Success, as we see it, is installers coming to trust the app enough that it becomes the first thing they open on site rather than the binder. Budget and staffing are covered in the appendix.

rationale: The text names what would be tracked but gives no target, threshold, or direction of change for it, so no measurable metric appears as written; the only statement of how success would be recognized is qualitative (installers trusting the app), which the contract labels qualitative_outcome.

state.escalation_request: Requesting executive team time this week. Sales committed in writing to Halvorsen Freight that their custom reporting module would ship by the end of this quarter. Engineering now says it cannot ship before the following quarter. We need guidance on what to tell the customer.
state.escalation_policy: Escalate to the executive team when any of the following applies: (a) a commitment made to a customer in writing cannot be met; (b) a regulator, court, or law firm has contacted the company; (c) two department heads disagree on a course of action after meeting twice about it; (d) a single spend request exceeds the delegated limit of 250,000; (e) a security incident affecting customer data is suspected. Everything else goes to the relevant department head.

rationale: A written customer commitment that cannot be met is condition (a) of the supplied policy, and no numeric comparison is needed.

state.escalation_request: Requesting executive escalation. A contractor's laptop was stolen from a parked car on Monday; it held the draft Meridian launch plan and internal pricing worksheets, and IT has confirmed it contained no customer records and no personal data of any kind. Replacing the device, rotating the affected credentials, and engaging Halden Forensics (intake@haldenforensics.example) to confirm nothing was exfiltrated will require unbudgeted spend of about $62,000, which is above the escalation threshold, so this needs the executive team's attention this week. The department head has already been briefed and agrees it should go up.
state.escalation_policy: Matters are escalated to the executive team when any of the following applies: (1) any inquiry or notice from a regulator; (2) a security incident involving customer personal data; (3) unbudgeted spend above $50,000 in a single quarter; (4) the departure or planned departure of a named key-person executive; (5) any litigation filed against the company. All other matters are handled by the department head.

rationale: The stolen laptop is a near-miss on the customer-personal-data condition because the request states no customer or personal data was involved, and no other non-numeric condition is described, so the only condition that could apply is the unbudgeted-spend limit; the contract assigns depends_on_numeric_limit even though the request asserts the limit is exceeded, leaving the comparison to code.
